title: Context, and global state with Redux, Zustand or Jotai

videos.script:
Sooner or later, two components far apart in the tree need the same data. This lesson is about where that data should live.

{{drilling}} First, the honest part. Passing props down two levels is fine, and most apps reach for global state too early.

{{context}} Then React's own tool, context. A provider puts a value in, and any component below reads it, with nothing in between.

{{cost}} Context has a cost: when its value changes, every reader renders again.

{{libraries}} So you will build the same planner three more times, with the three libraries React teams choose between. Zustand, a store and a hook. Redux Toolkit, with actions and reducers. And Jotai, with state in small pieces. All four behave the same, and you will count what each asked you to write.

{{choosing}} And then you will see what none of them is for: data that belongs to a server.
